clue.text: He lives here, writing science fiction

definitions.text: He lives here, writing science fiction

parts.words: He lives here, writing science fiction
parts.note: 'He lives here' sounds like a plain statement, but read as sci-fi jargon it describes a native of our planet as aliens would see him

explanation.surface: A novelist explains that he does his science-fiction writing at home.
explanation.definitionFit: In science fiction, a native of our planet is commonly called by this term, as opposed to Martians or other aliens.

clue.text: Serve coffee, forgetting nothing, and stirring in froth

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the remaining letters are jumbled
forgetting something leaves it out, so a letter is removed from the words

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A barista serves coffee and stirs in the milk froth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting nothing' removes an O from SERVE COFFEE, leaving SERVECFFEE, which 'stirring' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To effervesce is to fizz or bubble, which is what liquid does when it froths.

clue.text: Free, and threatening shortly to turn up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the letters from bottom to top
shortly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a dire warning is a threatening one

explanation.surface: Someone is released, though menacing signs suggest trouble will soon appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims DIRE to DIR, and 'to turn up' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone of a burden is to rid them of it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Out of the grip of alcohol, I'd a year's rest

indicators.note: the answer is drawn out from within the clutch of the following words, which hold it

explanation.surface: A recovering drinker says that, free of alcohol, they've had a year's respite.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through alcoHOL I'D A Year.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday is a break from work, a period of rest.

clue.text: Will provided for this married woman

definitions.text: Will provided for this married woman

parts.words: Will provided for this married woman
parts.note: Will looks like a legal testament, but it is also William Shakespeare, whose own will famously left his wife his second-best bed

explanation.surface: A testament made provision for a certain wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's wife is known chiefly from his will, which left her his 'second-best bed'.
explanation.definitionFit: She was the wife of William Shakespeare, the Will of the clue, and was provided for in his will.

clue.text: One possibly taking a poke at indistinct speech

definitions.meaning: someone who jabs or prods at another, such as a boxer

explanation.definitionFit: One who jabs is literally a jabber, while gabbled talk is also called by this word.

clue.text: Inform of an award for broadcasting

indicators.note: broadcast words are heard rather than seen, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: an award is a prize, so 'a prize'

explanation.surface: A notice tells someone about a broadcasting award.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprise someone is to tell them or give them notice, a synonym of inform.

clue.text: Excessively tanned girl is upset — brown, but a bit red

parts.note: skin tanned too much is burnt

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the pieces upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl is upset at being badly sunburnt, her skin brown with a reddish tinge.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an artists' pigment, a reddish-brown earth colour.

clue.text: List of bakery's product

explanation.definitionFit: A roll is both a register of names and a small individual bread from the baker.

clue.text: Such swindles may be trivial

definitions.meaning: a fiddle is a swindle, so such cheating is this sort

explanation.definitionFit: Petty cheating is called fiddling, and the same word means trifling or insignificant.

clue.text: Apparently 12, in certain cases, going up and down?

definitions.text: Apparently 12, in certain cases, going up and down?

parts.words: Apparently 12, in certain cases, going up and down?
parts.note: entry 12 means mad, but here is read literally as going round and twisting, as a staircase or rising and falling prices do

explanation.surface: A puzzle remark that the solution to 12 seems to apply to things that go up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 12-across, read literally rather than as 'mad', describes a coil that turns round and twists, like a staircase or an inflationary rise and fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A coil winding round and round describes a shape that goes up and down as a staircase does, or as prices do.

clue.text: Jack possibly raised cash mentioned for American horse

parts.note: a Union Jack hoisted is a flag flying, an example of a standard

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the sound of the word counts

parts.note: bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: A man called Jack raises money to buy a horse from America.
explanation.walkthrough: A jack is a ship's flag, and a flag raised on a pole is a standard.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a North American breed of horse used for harness racing.

clue.text: Mad Sixties' dance done after a few drinks

indicators.note: the dance is placed after the drinks

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group
the twist was a hit dance craze of the early 1960s

explanation.surface: After a few drinks, someone performs a crazy Sixties dance.
explanation.definitionFit: This British idiom means crazy, out of one's mind.

clue.text: How could one neglect the arts?

definitions.text: How could one neglect the arts?

parts.words: How could one neglect the arts?
parts.note: the arts here are crafts or skills, so neglecting them means acting without any expertise

explanation.surface: An indignant question about anyone ignoring culture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arts' suggests painting and music, but here it means skills, and neglecting them describes the manner of doing things clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without art or craft means doing it clumsily, with no expertise.

clue.text: In which many people are at cross purposes on specific issues

definitions.text: In which many people are at cross purposes on specific issues

parts.words: In which many people are at cross purposes on specific issues
parts.note: at cross purposes suggests disagreement, but read literally voters mark a cross on a ballot about one particular question

explanation.surface: A description of a situation where many people disagree on certain matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at cross purposes' seems to mean disagreeing, but voters mark crosses for the purpose of deciding one question.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a vote by the whole electorate on a single question, marked with crosses on ballot papers.

clue.text: What may be written in exam, for example, on einsteinium

definitions.text: What may be written in exam

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after

parts.note: Es is the chemical symbol for einsteinium
say is used to introduce an example

explanation.surface: A student writes about Einstein's element in an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition answering an exam question is a typical piece of written work.

clue.text: The fruit of something sinful get the point about it?

indicators.note: the point goes round the sin, enclosing it

parts.note: a tine is a point or prong, as of a fork
anger, or wrath, is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: A moral question asks whether the fruit of sin is understanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get the point' reads as 'understand', but 'about' has the point wrapped round one of the seven deadly sins.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small orange citrus fruit, like a mandarin.

clue.text: As part of tea, a pilot cooked sausage

indicators.note: the shuffled letters become part of the word for tea, sitting inside it

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are altered or doctored

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: At teatime an airman fries up a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As part of tea' looks like scene-setting, but it puts the anagram signalled by 'cooked' inside a slang word for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a small thin sausage.

clue.text: Team I'd set up in Australia finally lose, having become rusty

indicators.note: the team and the turned words are placed within Australia's short name

parts.note: Oz is a colloquial name for Australia
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a cricket or football team

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter

explanation.surface: A cricket team goes to Australia and ends up losing, out of practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses I'D, which follows the team; 'in' places both within Australia's nickname, then 'finally' adds the end of 'lose'.
explanation.definitionFit: To oxidize is to react with oxygen, as iron does when it turns rusty.

clue.text: Can retrospective, say, show a bit of colour?

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: looking back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: Would a retrospective exhibition show a splash of colour?
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace of a colour, a faint tint.

clue.text: Drink in oddly quiet US city

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the word is jumbled

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Having a drink in a strangely quiet American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like 'odd letters', but it rearranges QUIET to TEQUI.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Mexican spirit distilled from agave.

clue.text: Honest description of old-fashioned blonde

definitions.meaning: a blonde is fair-haired and an old-fashioned person is square, so someone both would be described this way

explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means honestly and without cheating, and literally it combines fair (blonde) and square (old-fashioned).

clue.text: Old MP, given reprimand, swallowing hard

indicators.note: one word takes in another, enclosing it

parts.note: to wig someone is old slang for scolding them, as in a wigging
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A former Member of Parliament is told off and has to take it hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Whigs were members of a British political party that later became the Liberals.
explanation.definitionFit: Whigs were members of a historic British parliamentary party, so one is an MP from long ago.

clue.text: Stop successful record from the past being included

indicators.note: the past piece is included inside the record

parts.note: a hit is a successful record
old means from former times

explanation.surface: A DJ is told to halt an oldie hit being put in the playlist.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase is a command to stop or wait, a synonym of halt.

clue.text: Journalist's work finally printed and bound for office

parts.note: a journalist writes an article

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A journalist's piece is printed and then sent to the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound for office' looks like 'heading to work', but it means tied by articles of training to a firm, as a trainee solicitor is.
explanation.definitionFit: An articled clerk is bound by a contract of apprenticeship to work in a professional office.

clue.text: Not certain leisure's sufficient to make a garland

indicators.note: not removes the next word's letters from the word that follows

parts.note: the word leisure as written, the possessive adding no letters
certain means sure

explanation.surface: Uncertain whether there is enough free time to make a garland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not certain' looks like 'unsure', but it takes SURE out of LEISURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers worn around the neck.

clue.text: Heard bloke spout

indicators.note: heard means the word is listened to, so the sound counts

parts.note: geezer is British slang for a man or bloke

explanation.surface: A man is overheard ranting.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the hot spring and the slang for a man sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A geyser is a natural hot spring that spouts water into the air.

clue.text: A view of Berkeley is mailed out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered or put out of place

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Berkeley viewpoint is sent out by post.
explanation.walkthrough: Berkeley is the Irish philosopher Bishop George Berkeley, not the Californian campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Berkeley's philosophy held that only minds and ideas exist, the doctrine known by this name.
